title: Spinach & Feta Frittata
instructions: Heat the oven to 200C / 400F.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper until just combined.
Heat the olive oil in a 25 cm oven-safe skillet over medium heat and soften the red onion for 3 minutes.
Add the spinach a handful at a time and cook until fully wilted, about 2 minutes. Spread it evenly across the pan.
Pour in the egg mixture, scatter the feta over the top and cook undisturbed for 3 minutes until the edges set.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 10-12 minutes, until the centre is just firm and the top is lightly golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, scatter with dill if using, then slice into wedges.
tips: Squeeze excess water out of the wilted spinach before adding the eggs or the frittata will weep.

title: Garlic & Chilli Spaghetti (Aglio e Olio)
instructions: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a cup of the pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat and add the sliced garlic.
Cook the garlic gently for 4-5 minutes until pale gold - do not let it brown or it turns bitter.
Stir in the chilli flakes and cook for 30 seconds more.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with 100 ml of the reserved pasta water and toss hard for 1 minute until the sauce clings.
Off the heat, stir through the parsley, season, and finish with parmesan if using.
tips: The starchy pasta water is what makes the oil emulsify into a sauce. Never skip it.

title: Thai Green Coconut Chicken Curry
instructions: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs clear, then cook it according to the packet while you make the curry.
Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a hot wide pan and fry for 2 minutes until it splits.
Add the green curry paste and fry for 2 minutes until deeply fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, cooking for 4 minutes until the outside turns opaque.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and bell pepper and simmer for a further 6-8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Season with the fish sauce, brown sugar and lime juice. Stir in the Thai basil and serve over the rice.
tips: Frying the paste in split coconut cream rather than oil is what separates a flat curry from a fragrant one.

title: One-Pot Chickpea & Tomato Stew
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a deep pot and cook the onion over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute until the spices smell toasted.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock, then bring to a simmer.
Add the chickpeas and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
Crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pot with a spoon to thicken the stew further.
Stir in the spinach if using and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Finish with the lemon juice and season to taste.
tips: Crushing some of the chickpeas gives you a creamy body without any cream or flour.

title: Crispy Black Bean Quesadillas
instructions: Mash the black beans roughly in a bowl with the cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt - leave plenty of texture.
Stir the diced red onion through the mashed beans.
Spread the bean mixture over half of each tortilla, top with grated cheddar and fold the tortilla over.
Melt a little butter in a dry skillet over medium heat.
Cook each quesadilla for 2-3 minutes per side, pressing down with a spatula, until deep golden and the cheese has melted.
Rest for 1 minute so the filling sets, then cut into wedges and serve with sour cream and coriander.
tips: Medium heat only. High heat browns the tortilla before the cheese has a chance to melt.

title: Chicken Teriyaki Donburi
instructions: Rinse and cook the short-grain rice, then keep it covered and warm.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and lay the chicken thighs skin-side down. Cook for 6-7 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Flip and cook for another 5 minutes, then pour off any excess fat from the pan.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 4-5 minutes, spooning it over the chicken, until it reduces to a glossy glaze.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, then slice it crosswise into strips.
Pile the rice into bowls, arrange the chicken on top, spoon over the remaining glaze and finish with spring onions and sesame seeds.
tips: If you have no sake, use an extra tablespoon of mirin and a splash of water.

title: Creamy Mushroom Risotto
instructions: Fry the mushrooms in half the butter over high heat in batches until deeply browned, then set them aside and season.
Lower the heat, add the olive oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until the grains look translucent at the edges.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it has almost fully evaporated.
Add the hot stock one ladleful at a time, stirring often and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
When the rice is creamy but still has a slight bite, stir the mushrooms back in.
Take the pan off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the parmesan, cover and rest for 2 minutes before serving with thyme.
tips: Cold stock stalls the cooking. Keep the stock at a bare simmer in a separate pan throughout.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken & Potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200C / 400F.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper together in a large bowl.
Add the chicken and potato wedges and toss until everything is thoroughly coated.
Tip it all into a large roasting tin in a single layer, chicken skin-side up, and pour the chicken stock around the edges.
Roast for 30 minutes, then baste everything with the pan juices.
Roast for a further 20 minutes until the chicken skin is browned and the potatoes are tender at the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes and spoon the pan juices over before serving.
tips: Do not crowd the tin. Use two tins if needed, or the potatoes steam instead of roasting.

title: Classic Shakshuka
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet and cook the onion and peppers over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes, season well, and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to hold a trench when you drag a spoon through it.
Make six wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one.
Cover the pan and cook on low for 5-7 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Scatter over the feta if using and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.
tips: Reduce the sauce properly before adding the eggs - a watery base will overcook the whites before it thickens.

title: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry

ingredients.quantity: 450 g, sliced thinly against the grain

instructions: Toss the sliced beef with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and 1 tbsp of the cornstarch and leave for 15 minutes.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce and cornstarch with the oyster sauce and beef stock to make the sauce.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 90 seconds, then drain it thoroughly.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok until smoking, then sear the beef in a single layer for 1 minute per side. Remove it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic and ginger, and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Return the beef and broccoli to the wok, pour in the sauce and toss for 1-2 minutes until it thickens and coats everything.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.
tips: The cornstarch coating on the beef (velveting) is what keeps thin slices tender under high heat.

title: Vegan Red Lentil Dal
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rinsed red lentils and the water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils collapse into a thick puree.
Stir in the coconut milk and garam masala and simmer for 3 more minutes.
Season with salt, finish with fresh coriander and serve with rice or flatbread.
tips: Stir the bottom of the pot regularly - red lentils catch and scorch easily once they break down.

title: Lemon Salmon & Asparagus Traybake
instructions: Heat the oven to 220C / 425F and line a baking tray.
Toss the asparagus and cherry tomatoes with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, the garlic, and half the salt and pepper. Spread them across the tray.
Roast the vegetables alone for 5 minutes.
Pat the salmon dry, rub it with the remaining oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper, and nestle the fillets among the vegetables skin-side down.
Lay the lemon slices over the salmon and return the tray to the oven.
Roast for 10-12 minutes, until the salmon flakes at the thickest point and the tomatoes have burst.
Scatter with dill and serve straight from the tray.
tips: Give the vegetables a 5-minute head start - salmon needs far less time than asparagus and will dry out if they go in together.

title: Chana Masala
instructions: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the onion over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until genuinely golden, not just translucent.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and fry for 30 seconds to bloom the spices in the oil.
Add the tomatoes and salt, then simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sauce darkens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Tip in the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Stir through the garam masala off the heat, then scatter with fresh coriander.
tips: Mashing a spoonful of the chickpeas is what turns a thin curry into a clinging one - no cream needed.

title: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 60 seconds, then drop it straight into cold water to lock in the colour.
Drain well, squeeze out the excess water and blend to a coarse puree with the green chilli.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the onion for 6-8 minutes until soft and lightly coloured.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, then stir in the cumin.
Pour in the spinach puree with the salt and simmer gently for 5 minutes - do not boil hard or it dulls.
Fold in the paneer cubes and warm through for 3-4 minutes, then finish with garam masala and cream if using.
tips: The cold-water shock after blanching is the whole trick - skip it and the curry turns army green.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions: Mix the yoghurt with 1 tsp garam masala, the paprika, turmeric, half the garlic and ginger, and the salt. Coat the chicken and leave for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the oven grill to high. Spread the chicken on a lined tray and grill for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a pan and fry the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the remaining garlic and ginger with the cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and darkened.
Stir in the cream and the remaining garam masala, then add the grilled chicken and any resting juices and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish with fresh coriander.
tips: Char the chicken separately before it meets the sauce. Simmering raw chicken in the gravy gives you stew, not tikka.

title: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Heat the oil in a wide pan and add the cumin seeds. Wait until they sizzle and darken slightly, about 30 seconds.
Add the onion and fry for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the turmeric and ground coriander, then the potatoes, and toss to coat every piece.
Cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally rather than stirring.
Add the cauliflower and salt, cover again and cook for 10-12 minutes until both vegetables are tender but still holding their shape.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and fresh coriander before serving.
tips: Shake the pan instead of stirring. A spoon breaks the cauliflower down into mush long before it is cooked through.

title: Rajma (Kidney Bean Curry)
instructions: Heat the oil and fry the onion over medium heat for 10 minutes until deep golden - this is where most of the flavour comes from.
Add the garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute, then add the cumin, coriander and chilli powder for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes and salt and cook for 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and the oil separates.
Add the kidney beans and 200 ml water, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash roughly a quarter of the beans against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Finish with garam masala and serve over basmati rice.
tips: Rajma tastes noticeably better the next day - the gravy keeps thickening as it sits.

title: Masala Omelette
instructions: Beat the eggs with the salt, turmeric and chilli powder until evenly coloured.
Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander.
Heat the oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Pour in the egg mixture and tilt the pan to spread it evenly.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the base is set and golden, then fold in half and cook for 1 minute more.
tips: Salt the eggs and let them sit for a minute before cooking - it gives a more tender set.

title: Vegetable Biryani

ingredients.quantity: a pinch, soaked in 3 tbsp warm milk

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak it for 20 minutes and drain.
Fry the sliced onion in the ghee over medium heat for 12-15 minutes until deep brown and crisp. Lift out half and reserve for the top.
Add the cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom and bay leaves to the pan and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and garam masala, then the vegetables, and cook for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat and fold in the yoghurt a spoonful at a time so it does not split.
Boil the rice in heavily salted water for exactly 5 minutes - it should still be firm - then drain.
Layer the par-cooked rice over the vegetables, scatter with the reserved onions, mint and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes before opening.
tips: The rice must come out of the water while still underdone. It finishes steaming in the pot, and rice boiled to tender first always collapses into mush.
